channel.accountConfig.configuredDetail: Token last 4: {suffix} · Updated {time} · Saving again creates a new token; the old token is no longer used
channel.accountConfig.credentialsHint: Channel API keys. Encrypted in Vault on save and never shown on the page.
channel.accountConfig.emptyDetail: No parameters or credentials yet; the account can't be activated
channel.accountConfig.entryRequired: Enter at least one parameter or credential.
channel.accountConfig.paramsHint: Non-sensitive business parameters such as outletRef or merchantId; keys 1–64 characters, values up to 8192.
channel.accountConfig.saveNote: On save, channel-connector encrypts everything with the CHANNEL_ACCOUNT_CONFIG_V1 structure and writes the account's Vault reference. Requires the "Account Credentials" button permission.
channel.accountConfig.savedNote: Saved parameters and credentials are never shown. To change them, click "Re-enter" and enter all parameters and credentials in full (this submission replaces the whole configuration).
channel.accountConfig.title: Account Configuration · {name}
channel.accountConfig.wizard.credentialH: Enter everything in full; values are never shown.
Current token …{suffix}. Enter everything in full; values are never shown.
channel.accountConfig.wizard.entered: {count, plural, one {# character entered} other {# characters entered}}
channel.accountConfig.wizard.note.oldTok: • The old token stays in Vault for audit and is no longer read. This submission replaces all parameters and credentials.
channel.accountConfig.wizard.note.replac: • Replaced immediately: once the new credential is saved, the next execution uses it; calls in progress are not affected.
channel.accountConfig.wizard.note.writeO: • Credentials are write-only: after saving, only the last 4 characters of the new token are shown. Field names may contain only letters, digits and _ . -.
channel.accountConfig.wizard.paramsHint: Non-sensitive parameters (such as region or language), referenced in atomic APIs as $'{'account.params.NAME'}'. Optional.
channel.api.cardFieldsHint: BODY string fields; can only be assigned card values from the card-reading initializer (PAYMENT_CARD) and are masked in execution traces and test evidence
channel.api.codePattern: Start with an uppercase letter; use uppercase letters, digits or underscores
channel.api.credentialFieldsHint: BODY string fields; can only be assigned from channel account credentials (resources.<initializer>.credentials.<name>), are masked in execution traces and test evidence, and the request body can no longer use sealJsonBody
channel.api.decimalEncodingHint: DECIMAL fields in channel messages: STRING as decimal strings / NUMBER as JSON numbers
channel.api.endpointRequired: Select one of the channel's outbound endpoints
channel.api.fixed.expressionHint: Write strings as 'application/json' and numbers directly as 100
channel.api.fixed.hint: Constants hard-coded into request fields per the channel protocol. Only constant expressions are allowed; they can't reference input, resources, steps or params. Once set, the field is read-only in nodes.
channel.api.fixed.title: Protocol Fixed Values
channel.api.hint.pathFieldUnused: PATH field {name} doesn't appear in the path template
channel.api.hint.pathVariableUnmatched: Path variable '{'{name}'}' has no matching PATH field
channel.api.noEndpoints: The channel has no outbound endpoints yet; configure one in Overview first
channel.api.noReferences: No standard API implementation references this API.
channel.api.outputs.errorFixed: Always an empty object '{}'; not configurable.
channel.api.outputs.hint: After status evaluation, outputs are mapped per branch and written to steps.<node>.outputs for the flow. A missing required output or a type mismatch turns the whole result into ERROR.
channel.api.outputs.valueHint: Can read http.* and params.* without protected handles. To take a value from an array, select the element explicitly with an expression, e.g. #http.responseBody.errors[0].code.
channel.api.params.hint: Values outside the message fields that a flow node supplies on each call. PROTECTED_HANDLE can only be passed to registered functions and never written into message fields, outputs or logs.
channel.api.pathVariableMissing: Variable '{'{name}'}' ✗ is missing a matching PATH field
channel.api.pathVariableOk: Variable '{'{name}'}' ✓ has a matching PATH field
channel.api.referencedSuffix: . When you change required request fields or delete this API, save validation lists these references.
channel.api.requestHint: Maintain the request structure row by row per the channel documentation; values are filled in flow nodes. Fields marked "Fixed" are supplied by protocol fixed values and can't be assigned by nodes.
channel.api.requestNote.header: HEADER names are case-insensitive; paths must be unique within a location.
channel.api.requestNote.path: PATH fields map one-to-one to the '{'variables'}' in the path template; values are encoded as a single path segment.
channel.api.requestNote.response: The "Response Fields" tab has the same structure and allows only HEADER and BODY.
channel.api.responseHint: Maintain the response structure per the channel documentation; types are checked whenever present, and required fields only when the result is SUCCESS.
channel.api.rules.hint: Evaluated in order; the first true rule decides the result. If all are false, the result is ERROR. There is no default "HTTP 200 means success" rule.
channel.api.rules.note.error: An expression error or a non-boolean result yields ERROR. After a SUCCESS decision, required response fields are checked; a missing required output turns the result into ERROR.
channel.api.rules.note.readable: Conditions can read {status}, {headers}, {body} and {params} (except protected handles).
channel.api.scripts.hint: Run in order. Script parameters can only take params.* or constants; protected handles can only be passed to registered functions, and scripts never see the plaintext.
channel.api.scripts.noneForStage: This channel has no {stage} shared scripts yet
channel.api.scripts.note.raw: Response signature verification reads the raw response bytes (http.responseRaw) and is not affected by response scripts modifying the working copy.
channel.api.scripts.note.referenced: When a referenced script changes its stage or parameters, saving validates and lists this API.
channel.api.scripts.requestTiming: After request assembly, before encoding and sending
channel.api.scripts.responseTiming: After response decoding, before status evaluation
channel.api.transportNote: The actual timeout is the smaller of the configured value and the flow's remaining budget. No automatic retries, no redirects, no cookies; Host, Content-Length and similar headers are handled by the system and can't be configured.
channel.capability.createNote: New capability groups are enabled; the six-dimension combination is unique within a MID.
channel.capability.detailsHint: Rendered from the capability catalog. ACTION.* indicates whether the action is supported; AMOUNT.MIN / MAX are per-transaction limits.
channel.capability.replaceNote: Saving replaces all details of this capability group.
channel.changes.manualIdNote: Changes to atomic APIs, shared scripts and standard API implementations are looked up by Owner row ID. Protocol lists show codes only, so IDs can't be selected yet.
channel.changes.pickObject: Select or enter an object to view.
channel.channels.accountActivateNote: Activation requires the channel to be ACTIVE and the account to have parameters and credentials written.
channel.channels.accountCloseNote: Closing is final. It is rejected while open MIDs are still bound to this account.
channel.channels.accountCreateNote: Created as DRAFT and unconfigured. It can be activated once parameters and credentials are written and the channel is active.
channel.channels.accountsEmpty: This channel has no channel accounts yet
channel.channels.accountsNote: An account's OE can't be changed after creation, and it can't be activated until parameters and credentials are configured. Credentials are never shown; only the token's last 4 characters are displayed. If "Activate" is rejected, the Owner's reason appears in the dialog.
channel.channels.capabilityGroups: {total, plural, one {# group} other {# groups}} · {enabled} enabled
channel.channels.codeExtra: Starts with an uppercase letter; A–Z, 0–9 and _ only; 2–64 characters. Globally unique and can't be changed after creation.
channel.channels.codePattern: Start with an uppercase letter; use uppercase letters, digits or underscores; 2–64 characters.
channel.channels.createNotePayment: Created as DRAFT; you can configure the protocol and run sandbox tests first. It can be activated once an outbound endpoint is configured. Payment channels are called by Payment through the payment entry.
channel.channels.createNoteService: Created as DRAFT; you can configure the protocol and run sandbox tests first. It can be activated once an outbound endpoint is configured. Internal services can call a service channel through the generic entry once it is active and authorized.
channel.channels.entityNoPattern: Two uppercase letters followed by three digits, e.g. AE001.
channel.channels.midsEmpty: This channel has no MIDs yet
channel.channels.status.activateNote: Activation prerequisite: an outbound endpoint is configured (same for payment and service channels). Otherwise the Owner rejects it and shows the reason. Credentials and standard API implementations don't block activation.
channel.channels.status.closeNote: Closing is final and can't be undone. It is rejected while the channel still has open channel accounts, credentials or MIDs.
channel.channels.status.grantsFailed: Couldn't load authorizations; this doesn't affect the action
channel.channels.status.reasonNote: The reason is written to change history; callers' rejection messages don't include it.
channel.channels.status.suspendPaymentNo: Once suspended, this channel's MIDs no longer take part in routing.
channel.channels.status.suspendServiceNo: Once suspended, all generic-entry calls to this channel are rejected immediately (channel not ACTIVE) and no external request is sent. Authorizations and credentials are kept; nothing needs reconfiguring after resuming.
channel.channels.status.title: {action} Channel · {code}
channel.channels.typeCard.payment.accoun: Channel accounts (bound to an OE; multiple allowed)
channel.channels.typeCard.payment.summar: Payment execution such as acquiring and refunds. Called by Payment through the payment entry; routing is frozen per OE and MID.
channel.channels.typeCard.service.creden: A single credential (not bound to an OE)
channel.channels.typeCard.service.summar: Third-party services such as maps, KYC, SMS and FX rates. Internal services call them through the generic entry, authorized per "caller × standard API".
channel.conflict.busyTitle: Save failed: someone else is saving this configuration
channel.conflict.changedTitle: Save failed: someone else changed this configuration
channel.conflict.detailHint: If someone else changed the configuration, reload and try again. Your input has been kept.
channel.conflict.kept: Your changes are still on the page and were not overwritten. You can reload the latest configuration and edit again.
channel.conflict.keptBusy: Your changes are still on the page and were not overwritten.
channel.copy.blocked: The browser doesn't allow writing to the clipboard
channel.cost.lifecycleNote: Lifecycle: DRAFT → submit → PENDING_APPROVAL → approve (ACTIVE if already due, otherwise APPROVED until the scheduled job switches it) / reject → REJECTED. Only APPROVED versions not yet effective can be voided to INACTIVE; an ACTIVE version can only be replaced by a new version. The approver can't be the maker and confirms the content hash when approving.
channel.cost.planCodePattern: Start with an uppercase letter; use uppercase letters, digits or underscores; up to 64 characters.
channel.cost.reviewNote: The approver can't be the maker. If the effective time has passed, approval makes it the current version immediately; otherwise it waits as APPROVED until due. A rejected version becomes REJECTED.
channel.cost.submitNote: Once submitted, the content is frozen and awaits approval. You're recorded as the maker, and you can't approve it yourself.
channel.cost.voidNote: Only APPROVED versions not yet effective (until {time}) can be voided. A voided version is final (INACTIVE) and never matches costs at any point in time.
channel.costEditor.effectiveFrom: Effective time (pick in local time; submitted as UTC)
channel.costEditor.midLoadFailed: Couldn't load this channel's ACTIVE MIDs, so the MID list is empty. Refresh later.
channel.costEditor.moreIssues: {count, plural, one {# more issue} other {# more issues}}
channel.costEditor.note: Rates are decimal ratios (0.0290 = 2.90%); amounts are decimals in major units, and entering an amount requires a component currency. Component types, calculation bases and rounding modes follow the channel-connector catalog.
channel.costEditor.title: New Version · {planCode}
channel.costEditor.versionNote: The version number is assigned by the system. The effective time must be later than the current version's. A new version can't be created while a DRAFT or PENDING_APPROVAL version exists.
channel.credential.activateNote: Activation requires the channel to be ACTIVE and the credential to be filled in. A service channel can have only 1 ACTIVE credential at a time.
channel.credential.closeNote: Closing is final. You can create a new credential afterwards.
channel.credential.configuredMeta: Configured · stored as a Vault token, last 4 only
channel.credential.createNote: Created as DRAFT and empty. It can be activated once parameters and credential are filled in and the channel is active. Service channel credentials are not bound to an OE.
channel.credential.disableNote: Once disabled, the generic entry no longer supplies account material; calls that reference the credential fail without sending a request.
channel.credential.empty: No credential yet. You can skip it if the external service doesn't require authentication.
channel.credential.notFilled: Not provided. Can't activate until configured.
channel.credential.note.disabled: • While the credential is disabled, the generic entry supplies no account material for this channel; atomic API calls that reference it fail without sending a request.
channel.credential.note.noPlaintext: • Plaintext never appears on the page, in API responses or in logs. Re-entering requires the full input; there is no "Show" button.
channel.credential.note.protect: • The credential is protected into Vault outside the channel-connector transaction; only the token and last 4 characters are stored.
channel.credential.note.reveal: • At execution, channel-connector reveals it under its own identity and uses it only in memory.
channel.credential.othersWarning: {count, plural, one {# more open credential record} other {# more open credential records}} ({records}). Only 1 can be ACTIVE at a time; activating a second one is rejected.
channel.credential.paramsNote: Encrypted together with the credential; the Owner never returns names or values. Atomic APIs reference them as $'{'account.params.NAME'}'.
channel.credential.single: A service channel has a single credential, not bound to an OE.
channel.delete.confirm: {code} (current version {version}) will be deleted. This can't be undone.
channel.delete.referencedHint: The configurations below still reference it. Remove those references first, then delete.
channel.delete.title: Delete {subject}
channel.diff.note: The comparison is aggregated in the BFF: aligned by six-dimension scope, then by component code. Any differing parameter counts as "Changed". Amounts and rates are compared numerically.
channel.diff.scopeColumn: Scope (MID / OE / Country / Currency / Payment Method / Action)
channel.diff.title: Compare Versions · v{target} ↔ v{base}
channel.editor.noProtocolPermission: You don't have permission to maintain protocol configuration
channel.editor.validationPassed: Validation passed. The configuration can be saved.
channel.endpointEditor.note.https: • https only. Format and IP literals are checked on save; at execution the address is resolved again and pinned before connecting.
channel.endpointEditor.note.trusted: • Mock addresses on this machine and mor-test are allowed by the channel-connector trusted-networks setting; the page offers no bypass switch.
channel.endpointEditor.note.version: • Saving increments the configuration version. On a concurrent change you'll see "Configuration changed by someone else" and your input is kept.
channel.endpointEditor.referencedHint: {count, plural, one {Referenced by # atomic API} other {Referenced by # atomic APIs}} ({apis}). It can't be deleted or renamed, but the URL can be changed.
channel.endpointEditor.sandboxConfirmCon: Once marked, sandbox test runs will actually call this endpoint. Make sure it is the channel's sandbox / test environment; marking a production endpoint as sandbox creates real transactions.
channel.endpointEditor.title: Edit Outbound Endpoints

channel.field.hint.pathDuplicate: Duplicate field path in the same location
channel.field.hint.scalarOnly: HEADER, QUERY and PATH can only be scalar types
channel.field.pathHint: Separate levels with dots and write array elements as [] (e.g. items[].sku). Paths must be unique within a location. Use STRING for exact values such as amounts.
channel.field.source.arrayHint: Array element fields can't have fixed values; a node assigns the whole array.
channel.field.source.fixedHint: Constant expression: write strings as 'text' and numbers as is; can't reference input, resources, steps or params. Once set, flow nodes can't assign this field.
channel.field.source.nodeHint: Assigned by a flow node in the request fields; optional fields are omitted when unassigned.

channel.flow.entryHint: Drag a connection from Start to set the entry node
channel.flow.entryMustBeApi: The entry must be an atomic API node
channel.flow.exits.hint: Evaluated in order; the first true condition is followed. "Otherwise" is always last.
channel.flow.exits.note: Conditions only read the context and aren't run on the page; an expression error makes the call return ERROR. Configure queries only when the channel agreement allows it; flows never orchestrate reversals.
channel.flow.exits.title: Exits of {id}
channel.flow.id.hint: IDs of initializers, nodes and exits are globally unique
channel.flow.id.label: ID
channel.flow.id.taken: This ID is already in use
channel.flow.initializer.handleHint: Protected handle; can only go to PROTECTED_HANDLE parameters
channel.flow.initializer.note.transactio: Runs outside the database transaction; results live only in memory for this call and are not cached.
channel.flow.initializer.note.vault: Reads Vault as channel-connector-service for the CHANNEL_EXECUTION purpose, and checks that the channel, account and Operating Entity match the inputs.
channel.flow.initializer.plainHint: Plain string; usable in request fields
channel.flow.initializer.requiredHint: On failure the call ends with 503 and no channel request is sent
channel.flow.initializer.title: Initializer {id}
channel.flow.leaveErrors: The flow still has {count, plural, one {# validation error} other {# validation errors}}; saving will fail and keep you on this page.
channel.flow.node.mappingHint: Click a row to edit it in the value popover; use "Field Mapping" to change several fields together.
channel.flow.node.title: Node {id}
channel.flow.node.unavailableSteps: Nodes not on every path are not readable: {steps}.
channel.flow.note.noCycle: Flows don't support cycles yet: connections back to an upstream node are rejected, and each node runs at most once per call.
channel.flow.note.publish: Takes effect for new calls immediately on save, with no publishing step; calls in progress use the configuration already loaded.
channel.flow.note.scope: Nodes can only reference this channel's atomic APIs; flows never orchestrate reversals, voids, refunds or other reverse money operations (manual review).
channel.flow.palette.apiDesc: Choose from this channel's atomic APIs
channel.flow.palette.fail: Returns a definite failure with outputs

channel.flow.sidebar.initializersHint: Run in dependency order before the flow nodes; if a required item fails, no channel request is sent.

channel.flow.value.handleHint: Protected handle parameters can only bind, by path, to credentials in initializer results.
channel.flow.value.pathHint: Read-only dotted path; indexes are not allowed. For array elements, select explicitly with an expression.

channel.grants.createEffect: Takes effect on save: {caller} can call {target} through the generic entry. If the channel is suspended, the credential disabled or the authorization disabled, calls are denied and no external request is sent.
channel.grants.disableNote: Once disabled, calls from {caller} to {api} return 403 CHANNEL_CALL_NOT_GRANTED. The record is kept and can be enabled again.
channel.grants.emptyWritable: No call authorizations yet. Click "New Authorization" to start.
channel.grants.enableNote: Once enabled, {caller} can call {channel} · {api} through the generic entry (the channel must be ACTIVE).
channel.grants.existsEnable: The authorization already exists ({status}, ID {id}), so none is created. Enable the existing record in the matrix.
channel.grants.existsView: The authorization already exists ({status}, ID {id}), so none is created. View the existing record in the matrix.
channel.grants.noImplementation: This channel has no standard API implementations yet
channel.grants.noImplementationNote: This channel has no standard API implementations yet. Implement a standard API under "Protocol" first, then authorize callers.
channel.grants.note.audit: • Every create, enable and disable is written to the channel change history (target type CHANNEL_CALL_GRANT). Authorizations can't be deleted.
channel.grants.note.columns: • Columns show only standard APIs implemented by this channel; disable the related authorizations before deleting an implementation.
channel.grants.note.identity: • Caller identity: with internal-auth on, the service name comes from the verified token; with it off, X-Caller-Service is trusted (transitional; must be on in production).
channel.grants.note.scope: • An authorization only decides whether a call is allowed; the channel must be ACTIVE and the credential usable for the call to be sent.
channel.grants.orphans: {count, plural, one {# more authorization points} other {# more authorizations point}} to a deleted standard API implementation. See the list view.
channel.grants.readOnly: Read-only: you don't have permission to manage call authorizations.
channel.grants.singleNote: Each caller × standard API has a single authorization. Re-enabling after disabling reuses the same record and increments its version.
channel.grants.subtitle: Allowed per "caller service × standard API". Unauthorized calls return 403 CHANNEL_CALL_NOT_GRANTED and no external request is sent.

channel.verify.account.entryLimit: Up to 64 entries; values up to 8192 characters
channel.verify.account.identityNote: Channel code, account ID and Operating Entity number are checked against the account identity in the case input when the flow initializes; cases can reference it directly with $'{'account.identity'}'.
channel.verify.account.noEntity: — (service channels are not bound to an OE)
channel.verify.account.noReferences: No test cases reference this account.
channel.verify.account.plaintextWarning: Test accounts are only used for sandbox test runs. By user decision, secrets are stored in plaintext in the channel-connector database; never enter production account material.
channel.verify.case.literalWarning: Expected values are compared literally; template variables are not replaced. To check a value from an earlier step, use "Exists" instead, or reference it in a later step's input.
channel.verify.case.note.literal: Template variables are replaced only in inputs. Expected values are compared literally; for cross-step consistency use "Exists" or reference the value in a later step's input.
channel.verify.case.note.negative: Negative cases expecting "Problem Before Execution" (e.g. 422) deliberately submit invalid input, so the input structure is not validated on save.
channel.verify.case.note.stringOnly: Variables can only appear in string values. When a whole string is a single variable it keeps its original type (such as object or number); embedded in text it is concatenated as a string.
channel.verify.case.oneOfPlaceholder: A, B or a JSON array
channel.verify.case.returnIdHint: Which exit the flow is expected to return from
channel.verify.case.staleWarning: Since the last pass, the case, test account or a referenced standard API / atomic API / script / flow changed. Run the test again.
channel.verify.case.standardApiHint: Standard APIs implemented by this channel
channel.verify.case.stepIdHint: Starts with a lowercase letter; later steps reference it as $'{'steps.<ID>...'}'
channel.verify.case.stepsHint: Up to 10 steps, run in order; if a step fails, later steps are skipped.
channel.verify.noPermission: You don't have permission to maintain sandbox tests
channel.verify.note.plaintext: Test account secrets are stored in plaintext by user decision and used only for test runs. Never enter production secrets.
channel.verify.note.sandbox: Tests only call outbound endpoints marked "Sandbox"; if an endpoint in use isn't marked sandbox, the run fails before sending any request.
channel.verify.note.stale: Runs are kept permanently. If a case, account or referenced configuration changes after passing, the status shows "Needs Re-test".
channel.verify.overviewEmpty: No test cases yet. Set up a test account first, then write cases step by step.
channel.verify.overviewHint: Test status of this page's cases, summarized by standard API
channel.verify.problem.inputObject: Input must be a JSON object
channel.verify.problem.statusInteger: Problem status must be an integer
channel.verify.run.hint: Uses the test account bound to the case and actually calls the channel's outbound endpoints marked as sandbox; nothing is sent if none is marked sandbox. The run happens in the background, and results and message evidence are saved.
channel.verify.run.reasonPlaceholder: e.g. regression after a channel upgrade

channel.verify.runDetail.skipped: An earlier step didn't pass, so this step wasn't run.
